analysis.title: Have European sovereign yields peaked?
key_insights: Germany's 10-year yield fell to 3.22% on 6 November, the lowest since late August and about 10 bps lower on the week. The move came with renewed weakness in global tech stocks, as investors sought high-quality bonds and cut expectations of further ECB hikes.
The French-German 10-year spread was near 155 bps, below its recent peak but still reflecting fiscal and political concerns. It recently reached almost 178 bps, the widest since 2011.
Eurozone inflation rose to 4% in October, mainly on higher energy and food costs. Core inflation stayed at 2.5%.

ECB President Lagarde said incoming indicators and the December staff projections will determine whether another rate increase is needed. Markets still price roughly an 80% probability of an ECB hike in December.

France's weak growth, negative rating outlook, fragmented parliament and obstacles to fiscal consolidation mean further spread widening remains possible. The weighted average cost of France's EUR 3.6tr debt stock is 1.9%, which slows the pass-through of higher yields to the interest bill.

High-quality bonds cushioned equity volatility during the tech sell-off. UBS says investors with large bond underweights can consider rebuilding strategic exposure, particularly in short- to medium-term high-quality government and corporate bonds.

UBS expects European borrowing costs to decline into next year and stays Attractive on European fixed income and equities, favouring short- to medium-term maturities including select agency, covered and corporate bonds and stronger investment grade issuers.

trade_ideas.description: Rebuild strategic exposure to short- to medium-term high-quality government and corporate bonds, including select agency, covered and corporate bonds and stronger investment grade issuers across medium maturities.
trade_ideas.rationale: Recent bond rally shows the diversification value of high-quality bonds, and UBS expects European borrowing costs to decline into next year.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy-driven inflation and France-specific fiscal and political risks could keep yields and spreads volatile.

risk_factors: Energy-driven inflation could force another ECB hike.
France's weak growth, negative rating outlook, fragmented parliament and fiscal consolidation obstacles could widen spreads further.
Yields and spreads may stay volatile.
vol_and_positioning: Global technology stocks are weak again, which drove demand for high-quality bonds. High-quality bonds cushioned equity volatility.
geopolitical: France's fragmented parliament and obstacles to fiscal consolidation, alongside a negative rating outlook, keep French spreads at risk of widening.
